title: Gray hulls hidden purpose
topic: Why the United States Navy painted its ship hulls gray during the Civil War (1861) to reduce visibility against the sea’s horizon

lines: A Union sailor slathers fresh paint on his ship’s side, sweat dripping.
His comrades snicker, saying the color is just for show.
At sunrise the fleet rolls out, cannon smoke rising, eyes scanning the horizon.
Confederate guns flash back, searching for any silhouette.
You see, it’s like wearing a gray hoodie on a foggy morning—hard to spot.
The Navy painted hulls gray to blend with the sea’s edge, making ships vanish against the distant line.
That camouflage reduced the chance of being sighted by enemy lookouts.
Ironically, the same shade helped friendly pilots find the fleet at night, because the gray reflected moonlight.

claims.claim: Camouflage on ships has been used since ancient times and continued into modern naval warfare.
